{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Exhibit 10.14)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement dated 5 February (Customer/AP — Kubient) 
**Status:** 19 rules assessed; 17 findings verified, 2 findings failed verification and are held for review

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. The commercial architecture is unusually favourable to us in several respects: the Vendor indemnity is broad and uncapped, there is no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-commitment or Customer-payable liquidated damages exposure, and the fee model is a revenue share rather than committed spend. We recommend no redline on those points.

The issues that warrant negotiation fall into two groups. First, **material gaps** — there is no monetary limitation of liability anywhere in the Agreement, no proprietary rights/ownership article covering deliverables and our data, no post-termination transition assistance or data-return obligation, and no Vendor insurance requirement. Given that Kubient hosts the platform and collects, stores and measures our data, the ownership, transition and insurance gaps are commercially significant. Second, **deviations from our preferred position** — the platform licence is expressly revocable at will and covers the Customer entity only; we have no convenience termination right during the Initial Term while Kubient has a mid-term "for any reason" exit; the post-Initial-Term exit requires 90 days' notice; governing law (Delaware) does not match the agreed New York exclusive venue; Kubient may assign freely, including to a competitor; and Kubient's warranties carry no remedy and no workmanlike standard.

Two findings (non-solicitation and audit rights) failed verification and should not be treated as settled conclusions. In both cases the underlying review reports that the Agreement is silent, and in both cases we would be *creating* a restriction on ourselves by inserting the playbook clause. We do not propose adding a non-solicit. The audit point is discretionary and low priority.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section (as reported) | Verified | Position / action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Missing | Preamble | Pass | No monetary cap on direct liability anywhere; add mutual cap at greater of 12 months' amounts or USD 1,000,000, keyed to amounts paid or payable between the Parties (the revenue-share model makes a Customer-fees cap illusory), with uncapped carve-outs and Section 5 payments excluded. |
| 2 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | Preamble | Pass | Broad Vendor indemnity in our favour, uncapped and carved out of the consequential-damages waiver; Customer-side indemnity is reciprocal and symmetric. No redline — reopening risks unravelling a bargain that favours us. |
| 3 | High | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | Preamble | Pass | No proprietary rights article. Add subsection confirming we own our Content, Properties and data; Kubient assigns deliverables with a perpetual royalty-free licence back for embedded Kubient IP; no joint ownership. No adverse assignment of our IP, so no walk-away trigger. |
| 4 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | Preamble | Pass | Licence is "revocable" and runs to the Customer entity only. Extend to affiliates and contractors, delete at-will revocability (revocable only on termination under the termination article), and permit transfer to a successor; retain the no-sublicence restriction. |
| 5 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | Preamble | Pass | No Customer convenience right in the Initial Term; Kubient has a mid-term "for any reason" exit on 90 days' notice; Kubient keeps all fees generated during the notice period and there is no pro-rata refund. Add a 30-day Customer convenience right with refund, remove the post-effective-date fee entitlement, and confine Kubient's convenience right to end of the then-current Term. |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | Preamble | Pass | Exclusivity expressly disclaimed; we remain free to sell Inventory through other agents or third parties. No redline. |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | Preamble | Pass | No non-compete, field-of-use or solicitation restraint binding us. No redline. |
| 8 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | Preamble | Pass | No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination fee against us; compensation is a revenue share of amounts actually generated. No redline. |
| 9 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Deviation | Preamble | Pass | Successive 1-year renewals (acceptable), but the only exit requires 90 days' notice — at the walk-away boundary and outside the preferred 30-day / fallback 60-day window. Shorten to 30 days, add an express non-renewal election, and require a 60-day Vendor renewal reminder. No uplift cap needed (revenue share, not fixed fee). |
| 10 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | Preamble | Pass | Termination effects cover cessation of Services, licence revocation and return of Confidential Information only — no wind-down assistance, no return of our Content, Requests or visitor data in usable format, no deletion certification. Insert playbook transition, data-return and certification language. |
| 11 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | Preamble | Pass | Warranty scope and duration meet or exceed our position and survive the disclaimer, but there is no remedy and no workmanlike standard. Add a professional/workmanlike warranty plus repair, replace, re-perform or refund at Kubient's option, expressed as non-exclusive of our other remedies. |
| 12 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | Preamble | Pass | Delaware law (fallback only) paired with New York exclusive jurisdiction. Change governing law to New York to match venue. No walk-away trigger (AAA arbitration, not seated abroad), but flag the conflict between mandatory arbitration and exclusive court jurisdiction for conforming. |
| 13 | Medium | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | Preamble | Pass | Mutual carve-out already gives us affiliate and successor freedom, and there is no change-of-control termination or re-pricing against us. Single gap: Kubient may assign to a competitor without consent. Take the fallback — narrow prohibition on assignment to a Customer competitor only. |
| 14 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | Preamble | Pass | No MFN obligation on us and none in our favour to preserve. No redline. |
| 15 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | Preamble | Pass | No take-or-pay, spend floor or volume commitment; fees track actual activity. Initial-term lock affects termination timing only and sits outside this rule. No redline. |
| 16 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review | Preamble | **Fail** | Full read reports no non-solicit, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant anywhere. Our preferred position is already met by silence; the deterministic sub-checks cannot pass because they presuppose a covenant. **We will not insert one.** Fallback held in reserve if Kubient proposes: mutual, personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months, general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, no no-hire. |
| 17 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | Preamble | Pass | No insurance provision. Kubient hosts and stores our data and Confidential Information and carries uncapped indemnity obligations. Add CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request; fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. |
| 18 | Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Needs review | Preamble | **Fail** | No audit right against us exists; the finding proposes inserting a bounded verification clause (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site, independent auditor, Vendor cost, no access to our systems) to pre-empt audit demands arising by implication from our use restrictions. Discretionary and low priority. Separately noted: Kubient measures Impressions and controls collections, and we have no reciprocal verification right — pursue as a Vendor-side records point. |

## Walk-away items

On the verified findings, **no walk-away trigger is currently engaged**, but two items sit close to the line and one gap is severe enough to be a condition of signature:

1. **Absence of any liability cap (Critical).** There is no monetary limit on either party's direct liability. While the uncapped Vendor indemnity favours us, our exposure is equally unbounded. We should treat insertion of a mutual cap with the standard carve-outs as a condition of signature.
2. **90-day post-Initial-Term exit notice (Medium).** The finding records this as sitting at the walk-away boundary and well outside our preferred 30-day and fallback 60-day windows. Combined with the absence of any Customer convenience right during the Initial Term, our exit flexibility is the weakest part of the deal. We should hold firm at 60 days at minimum.
3. **At-will revocable licence (High).** Kubient can withdraw platform access mid-Term. Removal of "revocable" is not a drafting preference; it goes to whether we have a usable service for the committed period.

Expressly **not** walk-away items, for the record: assignment (no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right against us, and no deemed-assignment clause); governing law and venue (AAA arbitration, not seated abroad); and IP (no affirmative assignment of our IP to Kubient).

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the eight actionable items with proposals: liability cap, proprietary rights, licence scope and revocability, termination for convenience, renewal notice, transition and data return, warranty remedy, governing law, assignment-to-competitor, and insurance.
2. **Sequence the negotiation.** Present the liability cap, licence revocability and termination/renewal package as the priority set; the insurance and assignment edits are narrow and should close quickly.
3. **Flag the arbitration/jurisdiction conflict** to Kubient for conforming at the same time as the governing-law change, so the dispute-resolution provisions are internally consistent.
4. **Do not raise the indemnity.** The allocation is symmetric and the Vendor side is uncapped and broader than our model language; we should not reopen it.
5. **Hold the two failed-verification findings.** No non-solicit will be proposed. Confirm with the deal team whether the discretionary audit-boundary clause is worth spending negotiating capital on; our default is to leave the Agreement silent.
6. **Open a separate Vendor-side records point** seeking a reciprocal right to verify Kubient's Impression measurement and collections, given the revenue-share model."}
